## Part 1
(25 points) 

Consider the language generated by the following context-free grammar.
Note that this language is defined over the alphabet $\{⌜a⌝, ⌜b⌝, ⌜c⌝, ⌜ϵ⌝, \varnothing, ∪, (, ), \{, \}, ·, ^{*}\}$.
Note, also, that $⌜ϵ⌝$ is an element of the alphabet, not the empty string.

::: {style="text-align: left;"}
$$
\begin{flalign*}
& S → (S ∪ S) & \\
& S → (S · S) & \\
& S → S^{*} & \\
& S → \varnothing & \\
& S → \{ T \} & \\
& T → T T & \\
& T → ⌜a⌝ ∣ ⌜b⌝ ∣ ⌜c⌝ ∣ ⌜ϵ⌝ &
\end{flalign*}
$$
:::

- How would you describe this language in words?
- Use the pumping lemma for regular languages to show that this language is not regular.

## Part 2
(15 points)

Consider, again, the languages (d), (e), and (f) described in @partee_mathematical_1990, Chapter 17, exercise 10.
For each of these three languages determine a pumping length $p$ meeting the description provided by the pumping lemma.
Justify your answer:
say why your choice of $p$ for each language is an appropriate pumping length.
